key_insight: A frontier LLM can generate and iteratively refine full, correct trapped-ion shuttling compilers from written specs, scaling from simple linear traps to general connected architectures.
engineering_relevance: This suggests much faster compiler development for new trapped-ion hardware layouts, cutting months of manual algorithm engineering down to days.
method: Started with an LLM-generated compiler for a linear segmented trap.
Seeded later versions with prior code to extend compilation to junction-based and then arbitrary connected trap graphs.
Benchmarked the generated compilers against hand-crafted state-of-the-art compilers on a common set of quantum circuits.
evidence_signal: Across benchmark circuits, the LLM-generated compilers reduced shuttling timesteps by up to 76% in linear traps and up to 39% with junctions, with strong architecture-dependent gains in the general graph case.
watch_item: Performance depends heavily on trap connectivity, so dense junction-rich layouts may benefit much more than corridor-like architectures.
paper_title: Efficient LLM-Generated Shuttling Compilers for Complex Trapped-Ion Architectures
